title: Read-only native Taskfleet children and the selected worker's conversation

state.description: working: Taskfleet runs the worker and its agent is at work. idle: Taskfleet still runs it, but the worker's own Pi session says its turn ended and it waits at its prompt for a person (an interactive run waiting for review, or a worker that stopped without finishing).

preserved.description: The ended run's branch or worktree is still on disk. In the list (no run query) an ended run appears only while this holds.

harness.description: The worker's agent: Pi, Claude Code, or another Taskfleet harness.

other_repository.description: The directory name of the worker's repository, present only when the parent conversation does not run inside it.

ended_at.description: When an ended run's Taskfleet manifest was last written, which is when it ended; absent while it runs.

awaiting_input.description: Taskfleet reads the worker as waiting for input at its own terminal prompt.

terminal.description: The live worker's Taskfleet window as the browser shell's read-only token (terminal.schema.json); only for the selected run, and only a pointer the terminal route checks again.

brief.description: The task Taskfleet gave the worker (its run's prompt); only for the selected run.

terminal_workspace.description: The workspace whose terminal route lists that window: the one holding the worker's worktree, which may be another than the parent's. Present exactly with terminal.

availability.description: available: the worker's native session was read. unavailable: not found (yet) or not readable. unsupported: Habitat reads no history of this harness.

entries.description: The newest part of the worker's native conversation as history entries. Tool-call arguments are inline (bounded); no block is read on demand.
